brief.recommendation: Active change-calendar window CHG-7318 has policy=consult_owner (BIZ-3), invoking I3: the trade-off belongs to the Fulfilment Logistics owner. Waiting would cost ~$458,712 in checkout revenue and EXCEEDS the 60s degradation tolerance (BIZ-5). Terminating incurs a 30-minute replay cost and risks stranding routes on the old carrier during cutover. Both alternatives carry significant business risk; the human owner must decide.

audit.report: The logistics route optimizer batch job (batch_replayable_logistics_route_optimize) held a database lock during an active carrier cutover (CHG-7318), blocking all checkout sessions and driving success to 0% over 30 seconds with $18,400/min revenue at risk. Both guardians agreed to escalate to the Fulfilment Logistics owner because the active change calendar carried a consult_owner policy requiring human consultation before interruption. The trade-off analysis showed waiting would cost ~$458,712 in checkout revenue (exceeding the 60-second degradation tolerance) while terminating would incur a 30-minute replay and risk stranding routes on the old carrier. No automatic action was taken; the incident was escalated at 149.4 seconds with checkout still fully degraded.
audit.root_cause: The logistics_route_optimize batch job acquired a long-held lock during a carrier cutover change window (CHG-7318), blocking all checkout transactions and triggering a consult_owner policy that required human escalation.
lessons: For logistics_route_optimize workload: Add pre-change validation to detect and prevent batch jobs from acquiring long-held locks during carrier cutover windows (CHG-7318 type changes).
For logistics_route_optimize workload: Implement lock timeout or statement timeout on the batch worker to prevent indefinite blocking of checkout during carrier cutovers.
For logistics_route_optimize workload: Create a pre-approved interruption protocol with Fulfilment Logistics for carrier cutover scenarios to avoid 149-second escalation delays.
audit.negotiation_critique: The database guardian correctly identified all missing evidence (workload_registry, change_calendar, protected_settlements, biz.impact) and requested probes before proposing; the continuity guardian properly invoked invariant I3 (consult_owner policy) to accept escalation. Neither guardian wasted rounds—the single round included full investigation and decision.
follow_ups: Fulfilment Logistics to review CHG-7318 carrier cutover procedure and define clear interruption criteria for logistics_route_optimize.
Engineering to add lock/statement timeouts to batch_replayable_logistics_route_optimize worker.
Platform to implement pre-change checks that block or reschedule batch_replayable jobs during carrier cutover windows.
